newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX hits 97 high despite steady blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX hits 97 high despite steady blue chips.

text.p: The SAX index hit a 1997 high of 205.58 points in flat trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, but traders predicted a stable trend for the bourse in the coming days.

Oil refiner Slovnaft, steel maker VSZ and bank VUB all closed unchanged, but recorded small rises in their average prices, while oil and gas storage firm Nafta closed up 20 crowns at 1,650 to boost the SAX.
"Currently blue chips are almost the only issues trading on the bourse, with significantly flat trading on the unlisted floor," Peter Lachkovic of Slovenska Sporitelna said.
Lachkovic said both Slovnaft and VSZ had some room for further gains, unlike Nafta, which gained on a volume of only 20 shares on Wednesday. "Nafta is deeply undervalued at the
moment, discouraging shareholders to offer their stocks."
Overall volume rose to 235,110 shares, from 234,465 shares traded on Tuesday, while turnover eased to 122.83 million crowns, from 223.42 million.
